content.value_statement: Object-oriented code can become hard to change and test. This skill explains SOLID principles with TypeScript examples and practical refactoring cues.
actual_capabilities: Explains the five SOLID principles in concise terms.
Shows bad and improved TypeScript examples for each principle.
Maps common code smells to specific SOLID violations.
Provides checklist questions for reviewing object-oriented designs.
Explains when to apply SOLID without over-engineering.
limitations: It does not execute or inspect a repository automatically.
Examples are TypeScript-focused and may need adaptation for other languages.
It does not cover every design pattern or architecture style.
Sample database code should be parameterized before reuse.

use_cases.title: Refactor a service class
use_cases.description: Split mixed responsibilities into focused services, validators, repositories, and report generators.

use_cases.title: Review object-oriented designs
use_cases.description: Use the SOLID checklist to identify tight coupling, broad interfaces, and fragile inheritance.

use_cases.title: Teach design principles
use_cases.description: Explain each principle with simple TypeScript examples and practical warning signs.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Principle
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the Single Responsibility Principle in simple terms. Give one small example and one sign that a class violates it.

prompt_templates.title: Find SOLID Smells
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this class design for SOLID violations. Identify the likely principle, explain the risk, and suggest a focused refactor.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me refactor this object-oriented module using SOLID principles. Keep the design simple and explain each tradeoff.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Architecture Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare two proposed designs against SOLID principles. Highlight extension points, substitution risks, dependency direction, and over-engineering risk.

output_examples.input: Review a user service that creates users, sends email, validates input, and builds reports.
output: SRP concern: the class has several reasons to change.
Suggested split: keep account creation separate from email, validation, and reporting.
Tradeoff: split responsibilities when they change independently.

output_examples.input: Assess a payment processor that uses conditionals for every payment type.
output: OCP concern: adding a new payment type requires modifying existing logic.
Suggested direction: define a payment method abstraction and add new implementations.
Review point: avoid abstractions until variation is real.

output_examples.input: Check whether a repository depends too directly on a database implementation.
output: DIP concern: high-level repository logic is tied to a concrete database class.
Suggested direction: depend on a database interface and inject the implementation.
Security note: use parameterized queries for database input.

best_practices: Apply SOLID when tests are hard, changes ripple, or variations repeat.
Prefer small abstractions that match existing domain behavior and names.
Keep instructional examples secure, especially around database input.
anti_patterns: Splitting every method into a new class before there is real change pressure.
Using inheritance where composition would make behavior contracts clearer.
Copying sample SQL with string interpolation into production code.

faq.question: What does this skill teach?
faq.answer: It teaches the five SOLID principles for object-oriented design and shows practical TypeScript examples.

faq.question: Can it review my whole codebase automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance for review prompts, but it does not scan files by itself.

faq.question: Which languages does it support best?
faq.answer: The examples use TypeScript. The principles also apply to many object-oriented languages.

faq.question: When should I apply SOLID?
faq.answer: Apply it when code is hard to test, changes spread across modules, or similar variations keep appearing.

faq.question: Can SOLID be overused?
faq.answer: Yes. Too many small abstractions can make code harder to follow.

faq.question: Does it include security guidance?
faq.answer: Only indirectly. Database examples should use parameterized queries before reuse.
